```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, weekofyear, count, expr, log

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("EventEntropyDemo")
    .master("local[*]")  # adjust for cluster
    .getOrCreate()

# 2️⃣ Load synthetic data
# Expected CSV columns: service_id,timestamp,metric,event_type,region,payload_size
synthetic_csv = "synthetic_events.csv"
df = spark.read.csv(synthetic_csv, header=True, inferSchema=True)

# 3️⃣ Pre‑process
# convert timestamp to timestamp type and extract week
from pyspark.sql.types import TimestampType
from pyspark.sql.functions import to_timestamp

schema = df.dtypes
casted = df.select(
    [col(c[0]).cast(c[1]) if c[1] != 'string' else col(c[0]) for c in schema]
)
casted = casted.withColumn("ts", to_timestamp(col("timestamp")))

# 4️⃣ Aggregate counts per service, week, event_type
agg = (casted
       .withColumn("week", weekofyear(col("ts")))
       .groupBy("service_id", "week", "event_type")
       .agg(count("event_type").alias("cnt")))

# 5️⃣ Calculate probabilities
# Total events per service/week
tot = agg.groupBy("service_id", "week").agg(expr("sum(cnt) as total"))
prob = agg.join(tot, ["service_id", "week"]).withColumn("p", col("cnt")/col("total"))

# 6️⃣ Shannon entropy (base e)
entropy = prob.groupBy("service_id", "week").agg(
    expr("sum(-p*log(p)) as entropy").alias("entropy_e")
)
# If you prefer base‑2:
entropy = entropy.withColumn("entropy_2", expr("entropy_e / log(2)"))

# 7️⃣ Persist output
entropy.toPandas().to_csv("entropy_output.csv", index=False)

print("Entropy output written to entropy_output.csv")
```
